messages:
Alex (support): Heads up — customer (acme-media) hit a big spike of 504/502s to the /generate endpoint starting ~22:04 UTC. They've been seeing ~15% request failures, mostly gateway timeouts. Request IDs: req=acme-7a2f, acme-7a34. They're on hosted inference in us-west-2 (dedicated pool: redwood-dedicated-gpu-a).

Priya (eng-oncall): Thanks Alex. Checking metrics now — grafana shows a sharp queue depth increase on the model-serving pods at 22:03. Pod count stayed flat for ~90s while arrival rate tripled. Warm start time (model init) for the slower pods is ~65-80s. That explains timeouts (gateway timeout threshold is 60s for this route).

Mateo (eng-sre): Can you paste HPA/KEDA config for that deployment? My guess: KEDA scaler threshold + HPA targetCPU are mismatched so KEDA didn't trigger fast enough and HPA scaled by CPU which trailed queue. Also want to see readiness/startupProbe settings — if readiness only becomes true after model init, new pods aren't counted for scaling in some configs.

Alex (support): Attaching snippets from the customer's namespace (sanitized):

```
# KEDA ScaledObject (sanitized)
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-queue-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: model-deployment
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
  - type: redis
    metadata:
      address: redis://redis:6379
      listName: inference-requests
      listLength: "50"
      activationListLength: "20"
      cooldownPeriod: "120"
```

```
# HPA (sanitized)
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-deployment-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: model-deployment
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 80
```

Alex (support): readiness/startupProbe currently: startupProbe=enabled, periodSeconds=10, failureThreshold=30 (so ~300s). readinessProbe disabled until startup finishes.

Priya (eng-oncall): Oh — startupProbe is long (300s) which prevents ready status until model finishes loading, but KEDA activationListLength is 20 and cooldown 120s. KEDA polls redis, but if the ScaledObject doesn't consider pods because they're not Ready, there's a race. Also HPA CPU target of 80% means CPU-driven scaling only after CPU rises — not ideal for queue-driven bursts.

Sam (infra): We saw similar before — KEDA scales based on external metrics but kube-scheduler and HPA interactions can cause scale delay. Two issues to fix: 1) Activation threshold too high (listLength 50) -> set activationListLength lower, 2) Consider using KEDA's 'polling interval' and 'minReplicaCount' bump during business hours. Immediate mitigation: bump minReplicaCount to 3 and set maxReplicaCount to 20 to give headroom.

Lina (customer-success): Customer is highly impacted. They've asked for a commit to reduce 5xxs or a mitigation within 30 minutes or they'll throttle traffic. They can't route to a fallback model. Can we give them ETA?

Priya (eng-oncall): Short-term mitigation plan (ETA ~15-25m):
- Patch KEDA ScaledObject minReplicaCount -> 3 (immediate).
- Reduce activationListLength to 10.
- Patch HPA minReplicas -> 3 and set target CPU -> 60.
- Add a temporary prewarm job (cronjob) to ensure at least one extra warmed pod is available per AZ.

Mateo (eng-sre): Longer-term fixes:
- Switch KEDA trigger to measure queue latency or use custom metric (avg processing latency) rather than list length alone.
- Add prewarm containers or a lightweight service that keeps model loaded in standby.
- Reduce startupProbe failureThreshold so readiness flips earlier (but watch for returning 503s if model isn't ready). Better: add a separate readinessProbe that checks health endpoint that returns 200 once model KV cache loaded to a minimal threshold.

Alex (support): I'll propose the quick patches to the customer. Deploy-bot will run the patch.

deploy-bot: Patch in progress: kubectl patch scaledobject model-queue-scaledobject --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":3,"triggers":[{"metadata":{"activationListLength":"10"}}]}}' (simulated)

keda-bot: Scaling event: detected list length spike -> triggered scale from 1 -> 4 over 40s; new pods scheduled but model-init times still ~60s, readiness pending.

Priya (eng-oncall): After the patch we saw errors drop from 15% -> ~3% within 6 minutes as queue drained. But a small tail of 504s persisted from a subset of older nodes seeing evictions and slow model-init. Looking at logs:

```
2026-03-15T22:05:18Z model-init: loading weights shard 3/8, memory pressure moderate
2026-03-15T22:05:54Z model-init: KV cache restored, warming prefix cache (estimated 45s)
2026-03-15T22:06:20Z readiness: still false, startupProbe failures=5
2026-03-15T22:06:55Z gateway: request req=acme-7a34 timed out after 60s -> 504
```

Mateo (eng-sre): Those logs show model init + prefix warmup contributes significantly. We should consider two changes: 1) change gateway timeout to 90s for heavy-model routes (short-term), 2) change model runtime to persist a lightweight 'fast start' mode (lazy load some layers). Both need product sign-off.

Sam (infra): Patch we applied to HPA and KEDA is live. I'll follow up with a ticket to change default ScaledObject activationListLength to 10 and reduce KEDA cooldown to 60s for inference workloads. Also will add a k8s annotation to prefer node pools with GPU preloaded images.

Lina (customer-success): Customer accepted the temporary mitigation and is seeing much better success rates. They're asking for a formal follow-up with root cause and timeline for permanent fix. I'll file a follow-up meeting.

Priya (eng-oncall): Action items:
- Mateo: create RFC for prewarm/standby instances + lazy load runtime (owner) — due EOW.
- Sam: infra defaults for ScaledObject -> activationListLength=10, cooldown=60s, set minReplicaCount default 2 for high-throughput customers — due next sprint.
- Alex/Lina: confirm customer acceptance and schedule postmortem meeting.
- Priya: adjust gateway timeout policy for the /generate route (ops-only change) and get PM approval.

Mateo (eng-sre): Also adding a reproducible test in staging: synthetic burst generator that simulates 3x traffic and measures scale latency and tail 5xx. Will include runbook and kibana queries.

Priya (eng-oncall): Closing note — root cause is combination of: queue-driven burst + KEDA activation thresholds + HPA CPU-driven scaling + long model warmup/startupProbe semantics. Not a single bug but configuration/architectural mismatch. Temporary mitigations reduced impact.

Alex (support): Customer thanked the team and will hold off escalation. Marking thread resolved unless new signs. :thumbsup:
